notes.content: The page questions the direct interpretability of << in terms of deployments and multideployments, and specifically says that G << F does not imply the corresponding comparison of Fig objects. It then records the data in terms of M: a family of subsets with an order implied by inclusion. The author finds that description less immediately congenial, announces the use of the grandes ombres, and begins a revised first axiom: a family of préadmissible sets of support M gives a preorder in M. The last sentence continues onto another page; that continuation was not consulted.
math_reading_decisions: The first Fig(F) has no index. The two following Fig terms and the final = Fig(F) each have their own M index.
All ten main-text M occurrences, all four main-text family F occurrences, the single powerset P and the separate uncertain marginal F were recorded individually where witnesses differ.
Subset has no lower equality bar; << has two left-pointing angle components; the two displayed/final non-strict comparisons use a straight lower bar.
The adjective impliquée is underlined, and the order is said to be implied by inclusion, not conversely. This is a reading, not a proof check.
The (1.33) frame is open on the right with separate strokes and left-corner gaps. It is an aligned definition list, not a diagram of relationships.
The lower citation literally has a point after 33; its closing sign remains )/].
Overlapped F/parenthesis alternatives and the foot numeral/closing-stroke alternatives are represented in place; no unsupported predecessor letter was invented.
H is credited for its notes correctly describing double underlining of pré, diagonal cancellation of the lower margin note, and a plausible 16 at the foot.

coordinate_convention: All crop_box and locus_box coordinates are [left, top, right, bottom] in the original 1682 by 2362 whole image. For an actual crop, crop_box is the full evidence crop; locus_box, when supplied, is the tighter occurrence within it. For a half-settled locus, crop is null and crop_box is the tight adjudication rectangle.
limitations: One enhanced crop per still-open locus, with no second crop or second view of a settled image.

No OCR, external research, other pages, other reader files, proof verification or LaTeX compilation was used.
